analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and file metadata. No independently supported security regression appears in these test changes. scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py:164–174 adds assertions allowing dispatch only at current dev HEAD with environment dev, while preserving rejection of prod/staging and stale dev sources. Existing surrounding tests cover signed source provenance, immutable recovery artifacts, qualification prerequisites and fail-closed trusted outputs. These relate to A-005, A-011, A-017 and T-054; tests do not establish deployed authorization or qualification.
The scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py patch replaces push-only assertions with scheduled/manual dev-lane checks: head lines 124–135 constrain the scheduled gate's permissions and dispatch target; 180–267 test separate cancellation groups and fail-open release scheduling on API errors, divergence or malformed JSON. New subprocess execution uses a temporary fixed gh stub and synthetic inputs; no consumer data or actual credential is supplied. Head lines 300 and 314–320 assert signing timeout and runner placement. Existing Apple-signing, fan-helper identity, environment-secret isolation and serialized publication assertions remain.
Integration must verify these assertions against .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py, not provided here: especially current-dev/environment enforcement, actions:write use, compare completeness, and cancellation interactions with signing cleanup and publication. Fail-open scheduling is not itself fail-open source authorization. Missing workflow/API source limits conclusions about the actual release path; tests were not executed. No supplied change touches inference encryption, cache scoping, billing or privileged runtime controls.
